turns.question: Why did we switch sessions to JWT, and who did it?
turns.text:
The switch was made to fix database load. Issue #11, "Session table causes DB load spikes" (opened by dave), reported p95 DB CPU hitting 90% at login peaks because the sessions table was hot [1]. PR #1, "feat(auth): switch sessions to JWT," was authored by alice and closes that issue. Its description says the team replaced server-side sessions with short-lived JWTs because the session table was the main source of DB load; refresh tokens stay server-side [2]. The auth design doc matches this: short-lived JWTs (15 min) with server-side refresh tokens, decided in #1 after the DB load issue #11 [3].

Who did it: alice authored the change (PR #1), and the graph shows her as the author of the auth design doc as well. The graph does not record who reviewed PR #1. Follow-up work includes rotating the JWT signing keys (IDN-1, in progress, alice) and a login redirect loop fix from JWT expiry mid-session (PR #6, erin) [4].

turns.question: Why are invoice emails sometimes sent twice?
turns.text:
The graph doesn't confirm a root cause, but the working theory is a retry in the batch invoice job, which lacks an idempotency key.

- Issue #14, "Invoice emails sometimes sent twice," is open. It was seen twice in one month and may be the batch job retrying [1]. A comment says it is "probably the batch retry from #4; needs an idempotency key" [2].
- The fix is tracked as ticket PAY-6, "Invoice emails sent twice," which is in Todo, assigned to erin, and linked to issue #14 [3].
- PR #4, "perf(billing): batch invoice generation," introduced batching of invoices in groups of 500. It was merged and reviewed by erin [4].
- The Billing runbook says that if invoices are duplicated, you should check the batch retry [5].

So the likely cause is that batch invoice generation (PR #4) retries and resends emails, and nothing makes the send idempotent. The graph has no record of a confirmed fix or a postmortem.
